short: The New Year rescript of 1946 in which the emperor disowned his own divinity.
full:
Issued on 1 January 1946 as the Imperial Rescript on the Construction of a New Japan, and drafted in consultation with occupation officials, the statement declared that the bond between the throne and the people rested on mutual trust and affection and did not depend on legends and myths, nor on the false conception that the emperor is divine and the Japanese a race superior to others and destined to rule the world.

The wording was carefully limited. It rejected the modern state doctrine of the emperor as a living god without explicitly denying descent from Amaterasu, and at Hirohito's insistence it opened by quoting the Charter Oath of 1868, presenting democratisation as a return to Meiji intentions rather than an imposition. Contemporaries read it as a renunciation all the same. It removed the theological basis of State Shinto, which the occupation had already disestablished, helped make it politically possible to leave the emperor on the throne rather than try him, and cleared the ground for the constitution that redefined the office the following year.
